name: Crucible LL-4 'Peacekeeper'
description:
A pump-action 12-gauge shotgun designed exclusively for less-lethal ammunition — bean bag rounds, rubber slugs, and tear gas canisters. The Peacekeeper's barrel is rifled differently from standard shotguns to optimize the spin stabilization of flexible projectiles, and its action is painted bright orange to visually distinguish it from lethal-ammunition weapons. The visual distinction matters: in the chaos of a security operation, an operator reaching for the wrong shotgun is the difference between compliance and a funeral.

Crucible markets the LL-4 as the responsible choice for crowd control and civil disorder management. The weapon delivers impacts equivalent to a heavyweight boxer's punch at 30 meters, creating compliance through pain without the permanent consequences of ballistic weapons. This marketing elides the reality that 'less-lethal' is not 'non-lethal' — bean bag rounds have killed dozens of people in GLMZ, typically through cardiac arrest when rounds strike the chest, skull fractures when rounds strike the head, or internal organ damage from close-range impacts that exceed the weapon's designed minimum engagement distance.

The LL-4 is the weapon most commonly deployed against civilians in GLMZ because it provides a veneer of restraint. Security forces can fire into crowds with Peacekeepers and claim they used 'non-lethal force,' even when the rounds break ribs, rupture organs, and kill. The weapon's orange finish has become a symbol of corporate doublespeak — the bright color that says 'this is safe' while the projectile says otherwise.
specifications:
caliber: 12 gauge less-lethal
action: Pump-action
magazine: 7 rounds tubular
effective range: 10-40 meters
minimum safe range: 5 meters (closer risks lethal impact)
weight: 3.4 kg
length: 840mm
finish: High-visibility orange
tactical_use: Crowd dispersal, subject compliance, and riot suppression. Operators fire bean bag rounds at center mass to create pain compliance, or deploy tear gas canisters for area denial. The weapon's less-lethal classification allows deployment in scenarios where ballistic weapons would escalate political consequences.
cultural_context: The Peacekeeper's orange finish has become GLMZ's most recognizable symbol of corporate crowd control. Protest art frequently features the orange shotgun, and 'getting peaced' is slang for being hit by a bean bag round. The weapon's name is regarded as darkly ironic by communities that have experienced its 'peacekeeping' firsthand.
known_users: Corporate security across all major corponations
story_hooks: A protester was killed by a Peacekeeper round at a labor demonstration — the official report claims a minimum-distance violation, but the forensic evidence shows the round was fired from maximum range. The round was modified to be lethal at any distance, disguised as standard less-lethal ammunition.

A stockpile of LL-4 Peacekeepers has been stolen from a security depot. The weapons are being given away free in the Shelf — but the ammunition that came with them is live 12-gauge, not less-lethal. Someone is arming a community while maintaining plausible deniability.

physical_description.visual_profile: A pump-action shotgun with an unmistakable bright safety-orange finish dominating its entire receiver and foregrip, creating immediate visual distinction from lethal weapons. The profile is utilitarian and aggressive — compact, purpose-built, with a pronounced pump mechanism and reinforced action designed for repeated cycling of less-lethal loads. The barrel appears slightly longer than standard tactical shotguns, suggesting precision in projectile stabilization.
physical_description.dimensions: Length: 840mm overall | Barrel length: approximately 460mm | Width at receiver: 65mm | Height with sights: 180mm
physical_description.weight_description: Substantial but manageable — 3.4 kg (7.5 lbs) feels heavy enough to absorb recoil from less-lethal loads but light enough for sustained crowd-control operations. The weight distribution favors the shooter, settling slightly forward of the trigger guard.
physical_description.primary_material: Steel receiver with reinforced polymer furniture; barrel is cold-rolled steel optimized for rifling geometry. Pump handle utilizes glass-reinforced polymer with integrated heat dissipation channels.
physical_description.finish: High-visibility safety orange on all exposed metal and polymer surfaces — a corporate mandate that ironically obscures the weapon's lethal capability within its classification. The orange is automotive-grade enamel, matte rather than glossy, showing finger oils and dust easily. Steel beneath shows minor corrosion in typical field conditions.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant bright safety orange (Pantone 151 or equivalent) across receiver, pump handle, and magazine tube. Black polymer furniture on furniture and grips. Minimal chrome on internal components. Some operators apply black electrical tape over portions of the orange finish in the field, contradicting the manufacturer's safety protocol.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured black polymer grip with aggressive checkering — designed for gloved hands operating in wet or chaotic conditions. The pump handle features vertical grooves and a slight curve, naturally guiding the palm. No secondary grips; mounting points visible at 3 and 9 o'clock suggest aftermarket tactical accessories.
distinctive_features: Specialized rifled barrel with unique groove pattern visible at the muzzle — optimized for bean bag and rubber slug stabilization rather than traditional buckshot
Oversized pump handle with integrated charging indicator — a small witness mark showing chambered status
Breech-loading port with safety-orange surround emphasizing chamber status
Minimal iron sights — small ghost-ring rear and front post, low-profile to permit red-dot mounting
Heat vent slots along top of receiver running from ejection port to charging handle
Manufacturer's 'Peacekeeper' logo in black block letters on left receiver, with product tier designation
Serial number and legality stamps on underside of receiver in compliance with GLMZ corporate-security regulations
Magazine witness holes along tubular magazine — round count visible without unloading
Safety lever positioned unusually far forward, requiring deliberate manipulation to prevent accidental engagement
Corrosion spotting on steel components from repeated exposure to tear gas residue and weather
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Crucible Agricultural Consulting logo (stylized grain stalk in circle) stamped at 2 o'clock on receiver in black. 'LL-4 PEACEKEEPER' in block letters at 9 o'clock. Serial plate riveted to underside of receiver with 12-digit manufacturing code and compliance stamp. 'LESS-LETHAL ONLY' in small print above magazine tube.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but maintained — the bright orange finish shows heavy scuffing and wear from holster carry and repeated cycling. Minor dents in magazine tube from transport impacts. Polymer furniture displays micro-scratches from glove contact. Internals kept clean by professional operators (security contractors) but show accelerated wear from bean bag load friction. Optics mount shows salt-spray corrosion in coastal GLMZ operations.
